subject: G01 forigerimod / HSPA8
my_first_view: The curated INHIBITOR row on HSPA8 exists in ChEMBL_37 on the acetate record only (parent record has no mechanism rows). Forigerimod is P140, the phosphopeptide of U1-70K; the two cited papers show HSC70 binding (2009, cell-surface binding on activated T cells) and impaired HSC70 refolding plus lowered HSC70 and p62/LC3-II rise in lupus B cells (2010). Nothing about neural cells, CMA by name, or WWOX. HSC70 block sparing WWOX is a question, not a prediction: HSC70 also folds clients.
checked_against: ChEMBL jsonl in view/shareable_package/class_b (CHEMBL3989409 empty, CHEMBL3989801 INHIBITOR HSPA8); PubMed abstracts of the two references
producer_conclusion: KEPT_CONDITIONAL; mechanism row real; abstract-level only; both H_HARM and H_PROTECT arms stated
correction_or_finding: Action real; peptide identity right; caveat the producer could add: the 2009 paper describes P140 as binding a cell-surface HSC70, so intracellular access in neurons is an assay problem as well as brain exposure

subject: G02 lithium / IMPA1 rejection
my_first_view: Lithium suppressing PTZ seizures in Wwox-null is in the saved paper (LiCl 60 mg/kg i.p. x3 within 1 h; Figure 7d caption). The sign argument (IMPA1 inhibition is proconvulsant in Li-pilocarpine and inositol reverses it) is an analogy from another provocation, so it disfavours IMPA1 as the mediator; it cannot exclude it. The same paper also ran a pilocarpine model in Wwox mice, so the provocation difference is testable in-system.
producer_conclusion: REJECTED_INFORMATIVE for IMPA1 as mediator and lever, reopen if inositol reverses lithium
correction_or_finding: Wording: the label REJECTED is stronger than the evidence (the producer's own NEG-01 text says it only disfavours). Prefer DISFAVOURED_BY_SIGN_PRECEDENT. Also the INV-09 movement note says the IMPA1 result supports the concern that the effect is not WWOX-specific; it does not (that concern comes from the +/+ arm of Figure 7d, not from the IMPA1 sign argument)

subject: G03 tiratricol/liothyronine for glia/myelin

The defect is thyroid-hormone entry, not WWOX; abstract names 400 ng/g as the dose that normalised, 50 ng/g was a lower arm.

producer_conclusion: Precedent read correctly, window stated, WWOX thyroid-hormone defect not documented, KEPT_CONDITIONAL
correction_or_finding: Producer writes that 50 or 400 ng/g normalised; the abstract attributes normalisation to 400 ng/g. Fix the dose wording. Age window (first 3 postnatal weeks, started at birth) correctly carried

subject: chain meaning

A sign error for glue-type drugs: lenalidomide family carries CRBN sign -1 because one record (CHEMBL848) says INHIBITOR while the salt record says MODULATOR; lenalidomide, pomalidomide, thalidomide are CRBN neosubstrate recruiters, so 'CRBN -P(-)-> IKZF1' with an inhibitor sign predicts the wrong direction. 12 proposal rows have main target CRBN, none handed over.

subject: guard effect 223 of 1202 withdrawn
my_first_view: Arithmetic: 1202 - 223 + 13 = 992 rows, matches proposals_it21.tsv. Spot-checked 10 withdrawn rows (seed 21) against withheld_rows.tsv.gz: all 10 are withheld by the stated rule (republished ChEMBL claim without level, or ChEMBL record written at family/PPI level). 5 of the 10 are pharmacologically single-target and the withdrawal loses a true direction (nemolizumab IL31RA, brontictuzumab NOTCH1, voclosporin PPP3CA, amcinonide and fluorometholone NR3C1, ethynodiol PGR). 10 kept rows spot-checked (seed 7): sign and level agree with family_actions; one wrong-sign kept row (lenalidomide, C1).
producer_conclusion: Guards correct, unknown is not negative
correction_or_finding: The guard is conservative by design; 94 compounds have no surviving twin and keep only an undirected association. Consider a documented-by-name allow list for antibodies and single-antigen drugs, otherwise the module will systematically under-signal antibody and steroid classes. Not a correctness error
